text_fidelity_a:
Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit We're huge Lego fans in my house, so while it may not be fair, I couldn't help but compare Mega Bloks with Lego. We got a few kits to try out, but otherwise, we've only used Lego in the past(though quite a bit of it). Unfortunately, Mega Bloks has just fallen short, for me, and I wasn't overly impressed.

First of all, I've been spoiled to numbered bags. While this kit is divided into 4 separate bags, you have to open all of them and dump them out, because the pieces you need for each step could be in any of the bags. I prefer, if I'm using a kit, to have my steps divided by bags. It keeps thing from getting less jumbled and lost. It kind of made me wonder what the point of 4 bags were.

Second, these blocks just didn't go together smoothly. Some of them require a great deal of pressure to get attached. They hurt my fingers. I even snapped my finger between two of the blocks at one point trying to get pieces together. (Sad, but true.) My fingers ache after working with Mega Bloks, just because of the pressure I have to use to get them attached.

Third, the directions aren't as clear as I'd prefer. Sure, as an adult, I figured things out, but for the average child, the directions just make things harder than they have to be.

When I discovered that Mega Bloks were compatible with Lego, I was really excited. I thought that the block building world could open up to more options for me and my children. We're sticking with Lego, though! It seems more organized and the pieces are more reliable. (They have more of a perfect fit than we've experienced with Mega Bloks.)

IF you are a fan of Mega Bloks, this kit is cute! (I just found it a pain. Literally. To be fair, though, I probably would have enjoyed the whole experience more, minus the finger pain, if I wasn't so spoiled from better. It really is cute enough!)
text_fidelity_b: Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:

I can't prove that they were tampered with, the right numbers of cards were all there in the right proportions, but it sure feel like this is some kind of scam the way those packs fell apart.

tl;dr: Stay away, get your boosters from sealed product like sealed booster boxes, sealed fat packs or sealed holiday boxes instead; the packs I got in bagged bundles from my seller were fishy as hell.

Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs. Okay, so I got the kit and made the TWO potholders. I bought this kit because the loom was metal, and I'd read reviews and seen videos where the person's PLASTIC loom would break. So, what's the problem?
I really don't like how the loops slip off this loom, especially when you're getting towards completing the project. Pop, pop, pop go the loops - OFF the loom! This might be the nature of pot-holder looming, but I think the problem is the little spokes (hooks) are straight, so there's nothing to keep the loops from slipping off. They should be curved and WIDER at the top so the loops can't slide off. Towards the end, when you're crocheting the edges together, the last side can get completely unraveled.
THAT IS frustrating.
I'm going to try to find another loom.
Unfortunately, I looked at a lot looms before I bought this one, and they ALL seem to have the same design flaw.

Afterthought:
On a positive note: the loops are NOT polyester, but cotton, so the potholders came out nice 'n thick and heavy.
I can see why posters said they lasted a long time. They probably will.
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs.

text_fidelity_a:
FurReal Friends Hop `N Cuddle Tan Bunny The Furreal Friends Hop 'N Cuddle Bunny (Tan color) is a nice toy for a young child. Rabbits are one of the more popular animals with little kids, and a stuffed animal like this that the child can control is a great idea, particular for a young girl like my niece who is completely bunny-crazy, and may be too young to own the real thing.

The bunny has a switch with three settings located on the bottom hidden by a velcro slot. "Try Me," for temporary activity, "Off," and "On." The "on" switch activates the one minute sequence of crawling in a circle approximately 3 feet in diameter (going clockwise), with occasional stops, sitting up, and various noises that I suppose to the right young person could be considered endearing. The sequence lasts long enough for the bunny do do a little more than one circular loop. It worked just fine on our carpet. I haven't tried it on the hardwood.

The "on" sequence will stop after about a minute, but if you gently brush a switch located on the bunny's lower back near the tail, the sequence starts again. My niece quickly figured out the mechanism, and sleeps with the bunny next to her, occasionally pushing the button if she wanted some motion or sounds. It stops after a short while if she does not.

The construction seems reasonable. The faux fur has been sewn over a hard shell animatronic body. There are pink pads on the bottom of the bunny feet. So this bunny is not squishable, and may not give the best hugs. I clicked four stars on the durable, but of course it hasn't been in action long enough to judge this.

However, I have noticed that she prefers her animals to make friends with each other and converse. After quickly learning the geometry of the pattern, she sits another animal where she expects the bunny to be at the end of its circular path, then begins narrating the important commands, statements, and then, when the bunny finally gets to the other stuffed animal, friendly greetings are exchanged between the two stuffed acquaintances. Adorable.

White Mountain Puzzles Cereal Boxes - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle [[VIDEOID:71ea1b294d36e01c1968e8869d80c0f7]] I really liked this puzzle. It was a really cool puzzle to put together. There aren't any super easy parts to this puzzle, but there aren't any super difficult parts of this puzzle, either. It was probably medium difficulty all the way through, so this made for a really fun experience throughout the entire puzzle.

This is a piece of art by artist Charlie Girard, which depicts about thirty different cereals. I think that all of the cereal boxes in this art are about thirty or forty years old, and there are many cereals that aren't currently sold today. The artwork is very fun, and this puzzle inspired a lot more conversation than most puzzles do.

I liked how well the puzzle was manufactured. The puzzle back was a really cool dark blue-green color, even though my video doesn't show how awesome the color is. Also, the puzzle pieces were pretty large. Usually puzzle pieces are 0.42 square inches, and these puzzle pieces are 0.72 square inches.

All the cereals in this puzzle are: Twinkles, Wheat Chex, Toasties Corn Flakes, Corn Kix, Corn Bursts, Rice Honeys, Cocoa Krispies, Honey Comb, Sugar Smacks, Alpha-Bits, Frosted Rice, Frosty O's, Raisin Bran, Froot Loops, Sugar Frosted Flakes, Trix, Crispy Critters, Life, Sugar Jets, Sugar Pops, Wheaties, Grape-Nuts Flakes, Apple Jacks, Sugar Sparkled Rice Krinkles, Shredded Wheat, Cap'n Crunch, Corn Flakes, Cheerios, Sugar Crisp, Rice Krispies

Pros:
+High quality puzzle, with a cool color backing
+Large puzzle pieces
+Excellent, fun artwork
+A great conversation starter about memories of different cereals

Cons:
-This puzzle will make you hungry

Advantus 12 Inch Desktop World Globe with Blue Oceans (30502),13 W x 12 D x 15 H in Does a perfect globe exist? Probably it does, but I couldn’t afford it. I’m happy with this one although it isn’t perfect.
The good stuff: it came in a super sturdy box that held the globe stable during transport. (The manufacturer ships it, not Amazon.) The stand seems strong and sturdy, and of course I’m grateful for the 720° rotation. The colors are attractive. I even like the raised texture where there are mountain ranges. I’m glad that the United States is divided into states. Finally, although I’m not 100% educated on geography, I can say this globe is up-to-date enough for my purposes; for example, Sudan is divided into Sudan and South Sudan.
The less-good stuff: I’m surprised to see that Canada’s provinces are named, but not outlined! Unless the lines are just so fine that I can’t see them, you have to guess their boundaries. Some cities are identified in the US states, but I was really surprised to see that state capitals are not identified! I suppose some state capitals are named, but Austin Texas (where we live), Tallahassee Florida, and other states I’m familiar with have various cities but not their capitals identified! I also think that city placement is close, but not 100% accurate. Nevertheless, this globe will get a lot of use in homeschooling, and will serve our purposes. I would buy the same globe again if I needed to for some reason.
text_fidelity_b: Advantus 12 Inch Desktop World Globe with Blue Oceans (30502),13 W x 12 D x 15 H in

Ravensburger Labyrinth Family Board Game for Kids and Adults Age 7 and Up - Millions Sold, Easy to Learn and Play with Great Replay Value (26448) So....I'm Gen X and we played the original version some in college along with games like Risk and Stratego on weekends. It isnt quite a fluff game but it isnt very hard. I would think both children and adults would enjoy this game. A game adults can enjoy with their kids....or a fun starter game or game for chatting and having a beverage or three.

The best part is there is hardly any explanation needed to get started. Move tiles to open a path to get to the objects on your cards. And....block others from their goals. I love this game especially with 3 or 4 people instead of two. It requires some strategy but luck can make or break it, too.

Harry Potter version! Yes! Well...it is beautiful. The board looks wonderful! But in this version you are gathering "people" or characters rather than treasure items. The premise makes sense. Going through the maze that is Hogwarts gathering people ....you must match cards in your hands to pics on the tiles of the gameboard. Sounds AWESOME. In reality...it is kind of messy because some people look similar. Some people are the big characters...such as Harry or Snape....there were 3 I was like....who on earth is THIS and I thought I was a big fan. So....due to the pics on the game board being rather small....they are also color coded too. If your card is Harry with a blue border....Harry has a blue border on the game tile as well. But is there another character who looks very similar on the board with a blue border? Yes there is. So....yeah, it is really cool BUT pay good attention as the character pictures certainly are NOT as easy to discern as a scarab or diamond in the original. Hey...but it looks great!

I give this game 10 out of 10 because my gripes do not effect the game. If you are are a HP fan....and you already like or think you might like a labyrinth game...here ya go. This is 100% Ravensburg quality. The box is good quality as all the pieces. The box holds everything in the usual labyrinth organized way. Very nice.

At the price point....I really, really, really dont like wooden pegs. They are sort of big, bright and easy to move but I liked the Labyrinth version with the plastic characters NOT the one with wooden pegs. I have no idea WHY if your player piece coincides with a house....such as Slytherin....they didnt atleast make little plastic coats of armor for each house. I just hate generic pegs in fun games. But it doesnt make the game any better or worse. I saw some reviews where people complained about the card quality. It is the same it always has been. The cards are simply there to identify your next goal. This game doesnt require shuffling like Uno or slapping...or grabbing or swapping cards. They are perfectly fine.

Great game. Great Ravensburger quality. Dear Ravensburger.....I sure would love a Scooby Doo version with cool plastic player pieces!

I included pics and pics of game pieces from an earlier version of the original game
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Labyrinth Family Board Game for Kids and Adults Age 7 and Up - Millions Sold, Easy to Learn and Play with Great Replay Value (26448)

text_fidelity_a:
Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

The packaging indicated Callie is from Japan, and she definitely has more almond-shaped eyes than Meredith. Her light skin, brown hair (instead of black), and eye shape reminded my bi-racial girls of themselves. That is the true gift of doll lines that have unique face sculpts, to provide a mirror so all little girls can have a doll that resembles them, as well as a truly diverse line of dolls.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola DigiTools Paint Pack Okay first off -- you can just download the app for this product in your Apple or Android app store. It will be somewhat limited, including having some of the "backgrounds" aka digital coloring pages disabled. There are more than one DigiTools apps - I was able to unlock two of the currently available four with this set: Their paint app and their airbrush app. Other sets that include different tools can unlock the other two (including a 3D set). The App consists of the backgrounds and several solid colored canvases. Using the appropriate tool allows you to do things like paint, stamp included images onto your scene, roll paint or images along your painting. Staying true to the Crayola kid friendly tradition the app doesn't include any sort of advanced features (no layers, etc). Your tools, an eraser, and an undo button are all you will find here.

The tools (what you're really buying here) consists of a Stamper, a roller, a brush, and an airbrush. Basically all of these (except the brush) are just several stylus nubs embedded into plastic tools that are kid friendly. The brush looks just like a run of the mill cheap brush (I can see kids grabbing it to paint with for real so look out for that) but when you hold it properly it too works like a stylus.

If you or the kids graduate out of the app and decide that say they do want to use them on more advanced programs? Good news and bad news there... The good news is that since these are basically just kid friendly tablet tools, yes these work in others apps. The bad news is that if you plan to say drag the stamper across your screen to get three lines at once? That's not going to happen. The screen will see this same as if you are using two fingers at once. So, for example, when I used these tools in Sketchbook pro? The brush worked perfectly. The airbrush and roller tools worked IF I tilted them so that only one nub was touching the screen at a time (otherwise it thought I was trying to pinch in and out / zoom). The stamper tool, which has three nubs, was basically useless.

The brush (the most useful tool in the pack) is also what makes this overall a 4 not a 5 star tool. The bristles are very fragile, I used this set a couple of times, put them away in the included carrying case, went to draw again and hmm the bristles were all fanned out and bent back. I don't know that the brush will hold up long term, it's already the most finicky tool in the set. Still, a fun kid friendly set that adults will love too.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola DigiTools Paint Pack

QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits This is not a “puzzle”, but a “model”. I can only assume that they do not have a word for “model” in Chinese. Because Chinese companies always list items like this is a “puzzle” though it’s really not.

This model is made of wood. It shows to have 47 pieces. There are 3 boards with the cutout pieces. You’ll want to use caution when removing the pieces from the boards so that you do not break them. You remove the pieces from the boards as you go. The pieces are numbered on the instruction sheet, but not on the boards. So if you remove them all at 1st, it will make it very difficult to put the model together. I highly recommend you have either a razor blade or thin sharp knife available to help remove the pieces. If you simply use your fingers, you could easily break a piece.

I must admit that I am not a person who likes to build models. So it took me about an hour and ½ to put this together. It turned out okay, but not as perfect as the pictures. The shingles do not fit perfectly. Nonetheless I think it looks okay.

Also, when you get to pieces 12, 13, 14 and 15 which is part of instruction number 5… Those 4 pieces make a little platform. The way the instruction show it on instruction number 9, that platform sits inside section B. But if you place it there, then the top shingle portion sits on top of the platform and is not sturdy. If you don’t put that platform there, then the top piece see fits in to the bottom piece a which makes it sturdy. Then I use that platform as a base on the bottom to place the temple on top of. Written on that platform is “Temple of Serenity”. So because of that, I think it should go on the bottom is a base anyway. But of course you can do it anyway you want to.

An optional string of LED lights is included. Two AA batteries are required and not included.

As a bonus, there is also a small “Ellie House” which is 24 pieces.

This model is made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 30 bucks I think it is a bit expensive, but it is a unique and interesting item. Also, it comes in a nice cardboard box, which makes it easy for wrapping if you’re giving it as a gift.
text_fidelity_b: QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits

I had read some of the reviews about the tails tattering in the wind so I took a proactive approach. As soon as I received it I opened it and inspected.... all looked good. The other reviewers suggested putting tape on the ends of the tails...I got a bottle of good old fashioned Elmers white glue and rubbed it on both sides of the end of the tails..about 2 or 3 inches up and let it dry. Brickyard Building Blocks 177 Pieces Large Building Block Toys for Children Ages 1.5-5, Bulk Block Set, Compatible with Duplo (177 pcs) We like the Lego brand, but sometimes we need a lot of bricks without paying an exorbitant amount of money. The 1,100 piece kit from Building Bricks was exactly what we were looking for. The Big Questions:
1. Do they really work well with Lego Brand Legos?
Yes - they work very well. It's difficult to tell the difference if you're not really trying hard.
2. How much cheaper are they? Is it really worth it?
It's hard to compare exact pricing here because this set does not include wheels, doors or special pieces. If I had to choose a product to compare it to, I'd probably compare it with Lego's XXL Classic Box (https://www.amazon.com/10697-Building-Large-Creator-Pieces/dp/B00XJ5C4FW). When pricing per piece, the Lego box is about 5¢ per piece. And yes, you read that right. You're dolling out a nickel for every piece of plastic with Lego's brand stamped on it. :) Building Bricks runs about 3¢ per piece. So the answer is: It's almost half the price - very worth it if you're just needing a lot of standard pieces.
As a side note: We really liked the color choices Building Bricks made. They're perfect for expanding your Lego creation palette.
text_fidelity_b: Brickyard Building Blocks 177 Pieces Large Building Block Toys for Children Ages 1.5-5, Bulk Block Set, Compatible with Duplo (177 pcs)

Ludonaute Fantasy Flight Games LUCV01 Carta Imperia Victoria, Multicolor CIV is a very good small card game. It takes about a half hour to play, and is largely comprised of cards with silly cartoonish art on them representing science, military, culture and so forth. Basically, if it's in Sid Meier's Civilization, it has been boiled down and reduced to a small concept here.

The artwork is...interesting. Some people will love it's uniqueness, while others will find it to be off-putting. I tend to fall in the latter column - it doesn't look like it matches with the theme of the game at all. The player aids are good, but small (probably to fit in the box), and can be difficult to read. It would have been better, in my opinion, to put some more text on each individual card instead of trying to stuff all the text onto one very small aid.

These are quibbles. The game is fast, interesting, and offers some good decision-making along the way.

text_fidelity_a:
3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner I think this thing is awesome!

That said, I do have a couple of warnings to consider. First, it will get really expensive! The sticks don't go very far at all. (The package claims each 6 inch stick will give you 60 inches of play, so I'm going to assume we just need more practice to get that much, as I'm guessing most others will, too.) With this set, you'll get 2 packs of the sticks(48 total sticks...6 each of white, mint green, yellow, orange, blue, red, green, and grey). You'll use those up super quick! These sticks are biodegradable, BPA-free and labeled as "safe". From what I've read, you'll need these specific sticks to go with the 3Doodler.

Also, every time you put a new color stick through the pen, you'll be wasting a bit of the previous stick, unless it works into your design. The whole stick won't completely feed through until you put another one in there to push it on out.

It takes a great deal of practice to get anything worthwhile to turn out. I have 3 little boys and they all want a chance at practicing, so even more sticks are used up in that process. So far, we haven't came up with anything close to what is shown in the practice book, but none of us can call ourselves overly skilled in the artistic realm at this point in time.

All of that said, IF your budget allows for buying lots of sticks to go with this pen, it truly is awesome! (Or you could request packs of these sticks as grandparent presents for the kids.) ;) Letting a child use his/her imagination with this thing is an amazing opportunity, and I definitely recommend it. (I even recommend it for adults, too, because we all need a little childish fun every once in awhile!)

It's easy to use. Just charge it up with the included micro USB cable(or do like me and use your kindle charger), turn it on and wait for the light to turn green. Then, press the button to start it and press it again to stop it. Simple! As I mentioned earlier, there is a book with instructions and some ideas to practice and get started with the pen. There's no worries about getting burned. I tested it out, and while the plastic is a little warm when it first comes out, it's not even close to hot. This allows for a little wiggle room for moving around your design before it completely dries.

In the end, other than the sticks being a costly investment, this is a great little invention, and we've loved it so far!
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner

text_fidelity_a:
Magformers Magnets in Motion Set - Engineering Magnet Toys for Brain Development - 300 Pc Set I have bought three sets of magformers now for all of my grandchildren (3 to 14). Even toddlers can play with them because they are too large to swallow. They also like the solid shapes and colors of Magnatiles but those are more expensive. You can also get magnetic wooden blocks (Tegu) but those are really expensive so I haven't bought any.

The magformers are one of those toys that both kids and adults can sit and play with for an hour or longer. What I've noticed with three young grandkids together is that they each have their favorite pieces and styles of construction. One always creates vehicles, one creates houses, and the third makes towers. The colors and feel of the pieces are both soothing and exciting to work with.

Update: I had five kids and two adults playing with these recently and the person that seemed the most focused on building things is an MIT Neuroscientist. Once he built things following the guide, the kids quickly caught on and followed suit. I recommend that an adult work with the kids to begin with.

Regarding complaints about the magnets not working, if you snap together two piles of similarly shaped objects and then try to put the two piles together, sometimes the piles will reject each other. If you take one pile and start adding it to the other one at a time, all the pieces hold to each other. It seems as though the magnets must change polarity inside the plastic. I'd love a proper explanation.

I only recommend getting sets of 40 or more to have enough pieces to be creative. Wait for them to go on sale unless money is no object. Since all the grandkids took their sets home with them, I've bought a fourth set to keep at my house.

Addendum per request: I first chose these toys because of the brightly colored plastic material but soon discovered that having the pieces snap together and hold their shape is quite satisfying. While they don't take away from the joy of plain wooden blocks, they are different and allow you to vary how you play with them.

This particular kit is right for me because I'll have a crowd of five young children and many adults (thankfully two engineers) for two weeks over Christmas and I'll put this out on a large sofa table in the living room near the tree. That way the kids will feel like they have toys and waiting won't be so hard. It also incorporates many of the other kits you can buy separately so the kids can see specific types of builds.

Go to youtube and type in magformers to see how they are used. Construction is really that easy.
text_fidelity_b: Magformers Magnets in Motion Set - Engineering Magnet Toys for Brain Development - 300 Pc Set

Haktoys Jurassic Dinosaur Bubble Shooter Gun 2 Toy Guns with Lights 4 Bubble Refills and Batteries Included Gift for Toddlers Kids & Parties (2-Pack) Updating my review:

I was contacted from Haktoys and asked if they could send me replacements if I would agree to update my review. I said sure! I thought this was pretty cool on the company's part.

So here it is.

I just took them out of the box and gave them to my two children (ages 4 and 6). They loved them and all was well but I was going to wait a few days to make sure they didn't end up having the same problem the old ones did where they just stopped working. Then my son accidentally dropped his on the garage floor - he did NOT throw it, it slipped from his hand and fell. The head of his dinosaur broke off and he is now sobbing.

I really wanted to give this a stellar review after the company went through all the trouble of sending me not one but two replacements. And really nothing is supposed to last forever. His dinosaur lasted less than 10 minutes though.

(also, as an aside - my husband was very happy it no longer rawrs. I missed the roaring!)

__________OLD REVIEW of NOISE MAKING MODEL_____________
This thing is the coolest thing ever while it works (unless you get annoyed easily by hearing the same noise over and over but hopefully everyone is outside and the sound isn't too intense). The only problem I can tell is that there is nothing if the child does turn it upside down while the bubble goo is in there to keep the bubble goo from going to the battery compartment? I'm not sure - I haven't been able to get the battery door off to replace the batteries and see if that will make the bubbles go again.

My kids (preschoolers) of course turned the darned things upside down (which it says not to do and I told them not to do) and now everything works except the bubble blowing feature. Will change my review if a change of batteries fixes this... assuming I can ever get the battery compartment door off!

ThinkFun HypnoGraph Drawing Machine and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 8 and Up - Creates Mesmerizing Mechanical Art First, I recommend going to ThinkFun’s website and watch one of their setup videos because the directions that come in the box are missing some important steps. It was really frustrating trying to put this thing together the first time before I realized there were important steps missing in the written instructions.

The box I received said for ages 8 to Adult, but the picture on Amazon says for ages 14 to Adult. I believe this is a better product for older kids. The precision and accuracy needed to be successful with setting this up would frustrate a younger child. I’m going to try it in my 4th grade classroom and I foresee some loving it, and some getting really frustrated with it.

The really good thing about this is that eventually it becomes easier to setup as you practice and learn from it. So, once you play around with it and make some sloppy pictures, you start to make some really cool pictures. Once a child figures out how this works, they will be able to make tons of different pictures as they experiment with different combinations of gears.

text_fidelity_a: T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle T. S. Shure had a temporary design lapse with this product; probably, the worst coming out of this brand.  Excellent idea coupled with poor execution only increases the frustration one would feel about the product.  The idea of 'magnetic' pieces to help discover countries and continents is great; so is the use of some cutesy imagery that often is often ascribed to a particular country (the dragon shaped like the Great Wall of China is a clear standout).  But trying to cramp all kinds of information in a tiny board proved disastrous.  The pieces are cut with no logic - the sub-continent looks from another planet; the font size for the capitals is so tiny, the target audience will barely notice it;  there are random airplanes and ships distracting the overall map and adding no value.  The tiny pieces are clearly not to be allowed anywhere near babies (it is rated for 6-15 years, to be fair; though it will be a miracle if anyone in that age group will use this for more than a day).  On the positive, with the weak magnetic pull and cardboard-feeling tiny pieces are bound to be lost sooner or later. And then you could create a new game - "which country is missing?".  That may be a better use of this playboard;

The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games First and foremost, this is a LIVING card game. It is not a COLLECTIBLE card game. Big difference! The latter just means that you can buy new expansions to expand your gameplay / add mechanics / etc. The latter means you have to go and buy packs at the store in order to get newer and better cards. In a collectible card game, a billionaire can go and buy all the packs and have the best deck ever. In this game, everyone who buys the game (and its expansion cards) will be on even footing. I find collectible card games to be somewhat predatory given they're essentially like gambling. Okay, on to the review.

High level message is, not great but not bad either. If you love Lord of the Rings you'll have a better experience. If you're neutral on it, then you're not going to enjoy the complicated grind of learning how to play.

Pros
- Beautiful artwork
- Good use of the LOTR lore in the gameplay and story
- Decent length of games - assume 1 to 1.5 hours
- Pretty good mechanics, once you understand them

Cons
- Phew, this game is complicated. The first sign that it's complicated, is the fact that there are TWO rule books, each of hefty size. This is not the kind of game you whip out on game night with a bunch of casual players. You need other folks who are dedicated to play this game, willing to watch a YouTube video together, or something, and then willing to stumble around for the first hour to get this done.
- So many things to keep track of... there's spinners, dials, tokens... did I mention this game is complicated
text_fidelity_b: The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

Testors Decal Paper, Clear, Pack of 6 (9201) I'm giving this product 4-stars partly because what was in the envelope was not what I ordered (white not clear), and because the sheets are small and there are only 6 of them for the price. Having found a work-around so I could use white substrate, I find this decal material relatively easy to use and can say the end result is quite suitable.

Here's what produced the best results:
1) Printed the images (inkjet Epson ET) and let them dry at least over night.
2) Sprayed them with one coat Krylon Crystal Clear Acrylic Coating, and let that dry for an hour or so. Acrylic clear coat is essential to getting a high quality finished result.
3) Applied a second coat of the Krylon and let is dry for about an hour.
4) Cut the images very close to remove as much of the white backing as possible.
5) Placed the decal in water with the backing side in the water. The edges curled up and I had to hold them flat for a few seconds to get the decals to lay flat in the water.
6) When the edges of the decal substrate (what the image is printed on) began to curl away from the backing sheet, I removed the backing sheet with the now loosened decal from the water and gently slid the decal off the backing sheet and onto my project surface.
7) Patted the decal gently with tissue to remove excess water from under and around the decal.
8) Set the project aside and allowed all moisture to dry. This assures the decal is set onto the piece.
9) Sprayed the project with two top coats of Krylon, with about two hours between spraying. This assures the decal is not easily scratched or marred.

What DID NOT WORK was floating the decal design side down in the water. This wets the Krylon coat too much and when you slide the decal off the backing and onto the project, some ink leeches out into the water and moist Krylon creating a slimy, grayish muck and tends to ruin the graphic.

I also searching for another brand that offers more and larger sheets for just a little more money.
text_fidelity_b: Testors Decal Paper, Clear, Pack of 6 (9201)
